RagShortTexts: Carcassonne with its double circuit walls and 52 towers cemented royal Capetian control in.

Variants.Content: Following the Albigensian Crusade, Louis IX transformed the Cité de Carcassonne into a formidable royal fortress. Enclosed within inner and outer stone circuits punctuated by fifty-two crenelated towers and deep moats, its interlocking fields of fire sealed the Pyrenean frontier.
The ramparts of Carcassonne proclaimed the end of southern baronial independence. The king's seneschal commands the garrison, deterring any intrigue between local nobles and the Crown of Aragon.
Building those double walls emptied the quarry tithes of whole cantons. Common folk must live in the lower town; once the iron portcullis drops at dusk, crossbow sentries patrol through the dawn.
